Article Title: Raghav Chadha’s Delhi voter registration approved after due process: Poll body
Article Text:
Delhi poll body said Raghav Chadha’s voter registration in Rajinder Nagar was approved after the mandatory seven-day notice period, while AAP alleged irregularities

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Delhi poll body on Wednesday said BJP Rajya Sabha MP Raghav Chadha’s application to be added to the Delhi voter list was approved after due procedure, days after the AAP questioned his inclusion."As per record available, Raghav Chadha, MP (Rajya Sabha) applied for inclusion of his name in Form 6 in AC-39 (Rajinder Nagar) on August 26," news agency PTI quoted Delhi chief electoral officer as saying."The Form was approved by the Electoral Registration Officer of the AC-39 (Rajinder Nagar) after completion of mandatory notice period of 07 days," it added.The application, numbered U05039D6N2608261200000, was processed under the Election Commission’s prescribed procedure.The AAP, however, rejected the explanation and alleged that Chadha’s name was added to the electoral roll "through the back door". The party also questioned whether political pressure was involved.AAP national media-in-charge Anurag Dhanda demanded that Chadha’s Form 6 be made public and said citizens should be allowed to raise objections against it as they can for any ordinary voter.Dhanda claimed that Chadha’s name did not appear in any Form 6 received in Rajinder Nagar between September 1 and 7.He also questioned how Chadha’s name became the 747th entry when the draft roll had 746 voters and the final roll was yet to be published.The CEO office said eligible persons whose names are not on the electoral roll can seek inclusion by submitting Form 6 with the required documents.It also referred to the Election Commission’s May 14 guidelines on the Special Intensive Revision, which state that additions made during the SIR period would receive serial numbers continuing from the last entry in the draft electoral roll.
Article Summary: Delhi poll body said Raghav Chadha’s voter registration in Rajinder Nagar was approved after the mandatory seven-day notice period. AAP alleged that Chadha's name was added to the electoral roll "through the back door" The party also questioned whether political pressure was involved.

Article Title: Ajit Bharti moves Delhi high court against trial court order denying anticipatory bail in SC/ST act case
Article Text:
Ajit Bharti moves Delhi High Court against trial court order denying anticipatory bail in SC/ST act case

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Social media influencer and YouTuber Ajit Bharti has approached the Delhi high court seeking anticipatory bail in the SC/ST Act case registered against him over his comments concerning Chandrashekhar Azad Ravan, after a trial court denied him relief earlier this month.Bharti has challenged the September 7 order of a Delhi trial court which dismissed his anticipatory bail application.The trial court had declined Bharti's plea after holding that the material placed on record prima facie disclosed the ingredients of an offence under Section 3(1)(r) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989.It had further held that the bar under Section 18 of the SC/ST Act applied and, consequently, precluded the grant of anticipatory bail."For the foregoing reasons, this Court finds that the ingredients of an offence under Section 3(1)(r) of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 are prima facie disclosed on the material on record," the trial court had observed while dismissing the plea.Additional Sessions Judge Saurabh Partap Singh Laler of Patiala House Courts had passed the order on September 7 in connection with an FIR registered at North Avenue police station.Ajit Bharti Bail Order.pdfThe case concerns statements allegedly made by Bharti during a programme aired on social media. The complainant had alleged that certain remarks made during the programme were casteist and derogatory towards members of the Scheduled Caste community.Bharti had sought protection from arrest, contending that the allegations did not make out an offence under the SC/ST Act. It was argued on his behalf that the remarks had to be considered in their overall context and that custodial interrogation was not required as the material forming the basis of the case was already available in the public domain.The State and the complainant had opposed his anticipatory bail application.After examining the FIR, transcript and other material placed before it, the trial court concluded that a prima facie case under Section 3(1)(r) of the SC/ST Act was made out and dismissed the application.The court had, however, clarified that its observations were confined to the disposal of the anticipatory bail plea and should not be construed as an expression of opinion on the merits of the case.It had also made clear that the trial court dealing with the matter would not be influenced by any observations made in the bail order and that Bharti would remain free to seek appropriate remedies available under law if circumstances changed.
Article Summary: Bharti has challenged the September 7 order of a Delhi trial court which dismissed his anticipatory bail application. The case concerns statements allegedly made by Bharti during a programme aired on social media. The complainant had alleged that certain remarks made during the programme were casteist.

Article Title: 'Won’t tolerate slur on saffron': Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari warns at Jadavpur rally
Article Text:
CM Suvendu Adhikari at the ‘Gerua Samman Yatra’ on Wednesday





KOLKATA: CM Suvendu Adhikari on Wednesday warned that he would not tolerate any slur on saffron and asserted that he knew how to “cleanse” Jadavpur University of those who raised slogans demanding freedom for Kashmir and Palestine and offered “red salute” to slain Maoist functionary Kishenji.“I have come here only to issue a warning. In today’s West Bengal, where there is a spiritual awakening around saffron, we will not tolerate anyone uttering insulting words against or writing derogatory comments about it. This is my clear message,” Adhikari said after leading a 2.5-km “Gerua Samman Yatra” from Golpark to the 8B crossing in Jadavpur.Vowing strong action against certain wall graffiti at JU, Adhikari said: “I have taken an oath. I will uproot the ‘Kashmir demands azaadi’ gang and those who raise slogans such as ‘Free Palestine’ and ‘Red salute to Kishenji’ from Jadavpur, which houses a centre of excellence and is the land of Rishi Aurobindo.”He asserted, “Bengal’s chief minister knows how to cleanse the campus of them.”The CM said a three-day programme of Veda recitation will be held at the 8B intersection, followed by two ceremonies where Gita and Hanuman Chalisa will be read.“Hiranmayananda ji Maharaj is organising a three-day Ved Paath programme. I expect all nationalist people to participate in it,” Adhikari said in his six-minute speech.“A few days after that event, I will come here twice at the invitation of West Bengal Sanatan Sanskriti Parishad. I will come once to recite Gita and then to read Hanuman Chalisa to teach a lesson to those who are insulting the countrymen and the saffron colour despite staying in this country.”‘Gerua Samman Yatra’, organised to “protect the dignity of saffron”, was joined by BJP supporters from across Kolkata and some districts.It rally began at 4.35 pm after CM Adhikari garlanded a statue of Swami Vivekananda near Ramakrishna Mission Institute of Culture in Golpark. Moving along the south-bound flank of Raja Subodh Chandra Mullick Road, the rally reached the 8B intersection around 5.10 pm.Saffron flags fluttered above the crowd as the rallyists chanted “Jai Shri Ram”, “Bharat Mata ki jai” and “Sanataner joy hok”.Conch shells were blown to the accompaniment of ululation. At the 8B crossing, Vande Mataram and Gayatri Mantra were played before the CM’s speech.Naga sadhus were among those who walked. Adhikari, dressed in a saffron T-shirt and trousers, walked alongside industry minister Tapas Roy, Kartik Maharaj, Shanku Deb Panda and other party functionaries.The procession disrupted traffic across parts of south Kolkata for several hours. Autorickshaws stayed off the road, while buses on several routes were diverted.A large contingent of police and central forces was deployed along the route and outside JU. All gates of the campus along Raja SC Mullick Road were barricaded.The choice of Jadavpur for Gerua Samman Yatra added political significance to the mobilisation. Last month, Adhikari had led a programme titled “10,000 Voices for Vande Mataram” near JU, criticising slogans allegedly raised on the campus and questioning the nature of protests there.
Article Summary: ‘Gerua Samman Yatra’, organised to “protect the dignity of saffron”, was joined by BJP supporters from across Kolkata and some districts. It began at 4.35 pm after CM Adhikari garlanded a statue of Swami Vivekananda near Ramakrishna Mission Institute of Culture.

Article Title: 4-year-old sexually abused by school cab driver in Delhi
Article Text:
File photo used for representational purpose





NEW DELHI: Police have registered a case under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (Pocso) Act after a four-year-old girl accused her school-cab driver of sexually abusing her in west Delhi ’s Ranhola. The accused is absconding and efforts are under way to trace him.According to police, the matter came to light after the child repeatedly refused to go to school. Concerned by the change in her behaviour, her mother spoke to her, following which the girl allegedly disclosed that the cab driver had touched her inappropriately.The family approached police and lodged a complaint. The child was subsequently taken for a medical examination.Police said statements are being recorded and details of the school’s transport arrangements are also being verified.Teams have been conducting raids at multiple locations to trace and nab the accused.The incident comes weeks after a similar case was reported in outer Delhi’s Bawana, where a three-year-old girl was allegedly sexually assaulted by a school-cab driver. Police had arrested the accused in that case following a complaint by the child’s family.
Article Summary: A four-year-old girl has accused her school-cab driver of sexually abusing her. Police have registered a case under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (Pocso) Act. The accused is absconding and efforts are under way to trace him.

Article Title: Cracks within Sena? MLA accuses minister of shielding corrupt official
Article Text:
Gulabrao Patil

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:

TOI





A war of words has erupted within Shiv Sena over alleged corruption in Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM), with Paithan MLA Vilas Bhumre accusing water supply and sanitation minister Gulabrao Patil of protecting a tainted executive engineer. Patil said the official in question had already been suspended.Bhumre alleged that several complaints regarding substandard and incomplete JJM works in Paithan taluka went unaddressed despite an inquiry reportedly finding the official guilty. “JJM has been ruined in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar because of one corrupt executive engineer. Despite an inquiry establishing wrongdoing, no action was taken. It is beyond comprehension why the minister is shielding a corrupt official,” he said.The MLA warned that he would take up the issue with party chief and deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde , and CM Devendra Fadnavis , if needed. Rejecting suggestions of factional infighting, Bhumre said his demand was solely for action against those responsible for irregularities in the scheme.His father, Shiv Sena MP Sandipan Bhumre, also called for strict action against allegedly corrupt officials and contractors linked to JJM works.Responding to the allegations, Patil said the executive engineer in question had already been suspended. “There was no recent communication with Bhumre, so he may not be aware of the action taken. Due process has to be followed against any govt servant, and that takes time,” the minister toldBhumre, who has repeatedly raised the issue in the state legislature, has threatened to lead a protest march to Patil’s official residence during the upcoming assembly session. Patil, meanwhile, said officials would be directed to ensure effective implementation of JJM in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar.In Dec 2025, Patil had admitted in the assembly that irregularities were detected in 73 JJM works in the district after concerns were raised by Bhumre and two other MLAs.
Article Summary: Paithan MLA Vilas Bhumre accuses water supply and sanitation minister Gulabrao Patil of protecting a tainted executive engineer. Patil said the official in question had already been suspended. He admitted in the assembly that irregularities were detected in 73 JJM works in the district.

Article Title: Quack doctor detained in Maharashtra for practising medicine without registration
Article Text:
A 27-year-old quack doctor was detained by Panvel police after an inspection (Representative image)





NAVI MUMBAI: A 27-year-old quack doctor was detained by Panvel taluka police after a complaint was lodged by the medical officer of the Primary Health Centre at Ajivali village in Panvel taluka, following an inspection by health department officials at his illegal clinic in Kasalkhand village on Monday afternoon.The accused was identified as Noorul Huda Imamul Haq, who hails from West Bengal and resides in an MHADA building in India Bulls Township, Kon village, Panvel.Gajanan Ghadge, senior inspector of Panvel taluka police, informed that the complaint was lodged by medical officer Dr Sayali Mankar, 33, who inspected Haq's clinic in Kasalkhand village and found that he was an unqualified and unregistered medical practitioner allegedly practising modern medicine by posing as a doctor.He had been running the clinic and treating patients for the past one month, police said. The police seized medicines stocked at the clinic as evidence.Inspector Ghadge said, "We have invoked relevant sections of the Maharashtra Medical Practitioners Act, 1961, against the accused, which prohibit any person from practising medicine in the state unless their name is registered under the relevant statutory provisions and prescribe criminal penalties and fines for those who illegally practise medicine without valid registration. Under the law, the accused was served a notice under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), directing him to appear for inquiry when summoned and during the court proceedings. "
Article Summary: The accused was identified as Noorul Huda Imamul Haq, who hails from West Bengal. He had been running the clinic and treating patients for the past one month, police said. The police seized medicines stocked at the clinic as evidence.

Article Title: 'Grabbed hand and attempted to disrobe': Cab driver tries to assault woman passenger near Navi Mumbai airport
Article Text:
Police have registered a case and are searching for the accused driver (Representative image)





NAVI MUMBAI: A woman passenger travelling home after attending a party in Chembur allegedly faced molestation and an attempted assault by a cab driver who took the vehicle to a deserted road near Navi Mumbai airport late on Saturday night, police said on Sunday.The incident took place around 1.30am on the airport service road, about two kilometres from Navi Mumbai airport, police said. The accused allegedly stopped the cab on the pretext of drinking water before moving to the rear seat beside the woman, police said.According to the police, the woman was travelling to Panvel after a friend booked a cab for her following the party."The driver stopped the vehicle on the deserted service road, stepped out briefly, and then re-entered the car, sitting on the rear seat next to the woman. He allegedly grabbed her hand and attempted to disrobe her," said an official of the Navi Mumbai Police.The woman managed to break free and escape from the vehicle, following which the driver allegedly fled the spot.After the incident, the woman contacted her family and went to Panvel Police Station to lodge a complaint.Since the alleged incident took place within the jurisdiction of Navi Mumbai airport police station, Panvel police escorted her to the appropriate police station.Based on her complaint, Navi Mumbai Airport Police registered a case against the accused, identified as Mohammad Afzal Shaikh, under relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).Police have launched a search for Shaikh and are using technical intelligence to trace his whereabouts.Further investigation is underway.(With ANI inputs)(The victim's identity has not been revealed to protect her privacy as per Supreme court directives on cases related to sexual assault)
Article Summary: A woman passenger travelling home after attending a party in Chembur allegedly faced molestation and an attempted assault by a cab driver. The incident took place around 1.30am on the airport service road, about two kilometres from Navi Mumbai airport. The woman managed to break free and escape from the vehicle, following which the driver allegedly fled the spot.

Article Title: FIR lodged after 3,400 SIR forms found in Navi Mumbai shop; 5 BLOs suspended
Article Text:
An FIR was registered against Suraj Patil for illegally possessing voter enumeration forms





NAVI MUMBAI: The police have registered an FIR against Suraj Patil, a nodal BJP youth wing committee member, for illegally possessing and converting special intensive revision (SIR) voter enumeration forms for “personal use” and for breaking the maintenance of secrecy of voting under Section 314 of the BNS and Section 128 of the Representation of People Act.Section 314 of the BNS deals with dishonestly converting a movable property for own use, for which the punishment is at least two years imprisonment.The matter came to light on Thursday, after an advocate working for the Shiv Sena (UBT) noticed hundreds of original SIR forms lying at a photocopier’s shop in Kharghar. He alerted the police.The accused (Patil) had decamped from the Kharghar police station, leading to high drama throughout the night.Authorities seized 3,404 SIR forms, including 11 blank ones, of 11 polling stations from the photocopier’s shop next to the Ramsheth Thakur Public School in Sector 19, Kharghar, by Shiv Sena (UBT) nodal chief Balesh Bhojane.Five booth-level officers (BLOs) served with show-cause notices were suspended by the Panvel City Municipal Corporation (PCMC) chief Mangesh Chitale.They include three data entry operators working as booth-level officers from a private company, Saunik Integrated & Security Pvt Ltd, Bhayandar, engaged by the PCMC.Their names are Sulochana Mane, Prashant Mhatre and Rahul Bhagat.The Shiv Sena (UBT) had earlier warned the Panvel sub-divisional officer through a letter about various lapses in the electoral process.A two-member inquiry committee comprising a Panvel deputy municipal commissioner, Nanasaheb Kamathe, and an assistant electoral registration officer, has been formed to conduct a comprehensive probe.Bhojane said, “MLAs Jitendra Awhad and Rohit Pawar have tweeted the video regarding the original SIR forms at the Kharghar shop. We demand action against the Panvel SDO as he did not take preventive measures despite our complaint about forms filed at the BJP offices. The FIR was filed only after more than hundreds of our workers assembled at the police station.”After learning about the incident, Raigad district communication head of Shiv Sena (UBT) Prasad Bhoir lodged a complaint with the electoral registration officer.“Yesterday evening, the election registration office (ERO) received information that a person is xeroxing enumeration forms at a Xerox centre at Kharghar sector 19. Immediately, the assistant election registration officer visited the site and found that one Suraj Patil was holding around 3,400 enumeration forms and xeroxing it illegally,” Raigad district collector Kishan Javale said.
Article Summary: Police have registered an FIR against Suraj Patil, a nodal BJP youth wing committee member, for illegally possessing and converting voter enumeration forms. The matter came to light on Thursday, after an advocate working for the Shiv Sena (UBT) noticed hundreds of original SIR forms lying at a photocopier’s shop in Kharghar.

Article Title: Shiv Sena leader Rahul Gharat arrested in Palghar hospital doctor assault case
Article Text:
A Shiv Sena leader was arrested after a hospital ruckus involving injured Govindas

MLA seeks action against doctors





PALGHAR: Shiv Sena (Shinde faction) Palghar city chief Rahul Gharat, the main accused in the alleged ruckus and assault at a private hospital in Palghar, was arrested on Monday after he surrendered before the police.The incident took place at Relief Hospital in Palghar on Saturday night when five injured Govindas, who had sustained injuries during Dahi Handi celebrations, were admitted for treatment. Three of them were kept in the intensive care unit (ICU).The injured Govindas had alleged that the hospital was forcing them to undergo CT scans and was trying to charge them excessive amounts. Following the allegations, Shiv Sena office-bearers and workers entered the hospital late at night and allegedly created a ruckus. A hospital employee was assaulted and the IV lines of the Govindas admitted to the ICU were allegedly removed before they were taken away.Palghar police had registered a case against 17 people, including Shiv Sena district chief Kundan Sankhe, city chief Rahul Gharat, the son of MLA Rajendra Gavit and deputy taluka chief Rohit Gavit, under various sections of the law.“Gharat appeared before the Palghar police station on Monday and was arrested.Efforts are on to trace the remaining accused,” said Kishor Manbhav, senior police inspector of Palghar police station.Meanwhile, injured Govinda Akash Patil reiterated his allegations against the doctors. He claimed that although he felt better after being given an injection, he was allegedly kept in the ICU for three hours after being put on a saline drip against his wishes. He demanded action against the doctors.Palghar MLA Rajendra Gavit visited the Palghar police station on Monday and demanded that a case be registered against the doctors.Gavit alleged that the hospital staff were forcing the injured Govindas to stay back and undergo MRI and CT scans. He said Shiv Sena workers had gone to the hospital to help the injured Govindas and that a verbal altercation had taken place.He alleged that the doctors had filed a complaint against the Shiv Sena workers out of vendetta and pressured the police to register a case. “Can a patient not even question a doctor about an excessive bill?” Gavit asked, demanding that the police register a case against the doctors.
Article Summary: Palghar city chief Rahul Gharat, the main accused in the alleged ruckus and assault at a private hospital in Palghar, was arrested on Monday. The incident took place at Relief Hospital on Saturday night when five injured Govindas, who had sustained injuries during Dahi Handi celebrations, were admitted for treatment. Three of them were kept in the intensive care unit.

Article Title: 'Minor injuries, kept in ICU': Govinda group file FIR against Palghar doctor, threaten sit-in outside police station
Article Text:
Sena’s district chief Kundan Sankhe claimed they went to Relief Hospital after receiving complaints that the govindas were not being allowed to leave





PALGHAR: A fresh twist has emerged in the alleged assault of a receptionist at Relief Hospital in Palghar, with the injured Govinda participants whose treatment triggered the dispute filing a written complaint against the doctor at Palghar police station.A case has already been registered against 17 people, including Shiv Sena district chief Kundan Sankhe, in connection with the alleged assault.In their complaint, the Govinda participants alleged that although they had suffered only minor injuries, they were deliberately kept in the ICU and were not discharged despite repeatedly requesting the doctor to release them.They further alleged that the doctor ignored their requests, following which they sought the intervention of Sankhe. The participants claimed that unnecessary treatment was continued despite there being no medical requirement for it.The complainants have demanded that a case be registered against the doctor over the alleged conduct.Palghar MLA Rajendra Gavit, along with senior Shiv Sena functionaries, party workers and members of the Govinda group, gathered outside Palghar police station in support of the complaint.Gavit warned that the group would stage a sit-in outside the police station until a case was registered against the doctor.The latest complaint comes amid the ongoing controversy over the alleged assault of the hospital receptionist and the case registered against Sankhe and others.
Article Summary: Govinda participants claim they were deliberately kept in the ICU and were not discharged despite repeatedly requesting the doctor to release them. A case has already been registered against 17 people, including Shiv Sena district chief Kundan Sankhe, in connection with the alleged assault.

Article Title: ACB arrests assistant police inspector for demanding & accepting bribe
Article Text:
Pune:





The state anti-corruption bureau (ACB) arrested an assistant police inspector attached to Loni Kalbhor police station for allegedly demanding a Rs 2.5 lakh bribe and accepting Rs 50,000 late on Tuesday night in Manjari near Hadapsar.The arrested officer was identified as Krushna Janardhan Babar (45), a resident of Manjari. The ACB has registered a case against him at Hadapsar police station.According to the ACB, the Loni Kalbhor police had registered a cheating case against a 57-year-old man and his son from Hadapsar, which Babar was investigating. The man, who is also the complainant in the bribery case, approached Babar a few days ago and requested him to submit the chargesheet in court at the earliest.“Babar allegedly demanded Rs 50,000 to expedite the filing of the chargesheet and another Rs 2 lakh to help the accused obtain anticipatory bail and provide further assistance in the case,” an ACB official said.The complainant handed over Rs 50,000 to Babar on Tuesday night, following which ACB officials caught the officer red-handed.
Article Summary: The arrested officer was identified as Krushna Janardhan Babar (45), a resident of Manjari. The ACB has registered a case against him at Hadapsar police station. The Loni Kalbhor police had registered a cheating case against a 57-year-old man and his son.

Article Title: 15 chain-snatching cases detected; two held, gold jewellery worth Rs35.33 lakh recovered
Article Text:
Pimpri Chinchwad police commissioner Vinoy Kumar Choubey felicitates crime branch team for detecting 15 chain snatching cases

Pune:





Pimpri Chinchwad crime branch on Wednesday claimed to have detected 15 chain-snatching cases with the arrest of a habitual chain snatcher and his accomplice.The police recovered 27 tolas of gold jewellery worth Rs35.33 lakh from the accused, Fida Hussain Irani (33), and his accomplice, Mukesh Netke (38), both residents of Patil Estate in Shivajinagar. A crime branch team led by senior police inspector Sanjay Chavan arrested the duo after examining footage from more than 500 CCTV cameras.On May 12, two men riding a motorcycle snatched a gold chain worth Rs90,000 from a 41-year-old nurse at Nigdi Pradhikaran. The woman later lodged a complaint with the Nigdi police. Deputy commissioner of police (crime) Rohidas Pawar of the Pimpri Chinchwad police said that an examination of the CCTV footage showed that after snatching the chain, the duo fled towards Mumbai. They were wearing helmets and had covered their faces with masks. The snatchers used sports bikes to commit the crimes. “With the help of CCTV footage, technical investigation and a tip-off, inspector Chavan and his team ascertained the identity of the snatcher as Fida Irani,” Pawar said.The DCP said the police received a tip-off that Irani would be coming to Dehu Road on Sept 5. “We nabbed Irani and Netke from Dehu Road,” Pawar said.He said that during sustained interrogation, Irani admitted to having snatched 15 gold chains over the past few months with the help of three accomplices. “Of the 15 cases, 13 were registered with the Pimpri Chinchwad police and two with the Pune police,” he said.Pawar said Irani is wanted in five more chain-snatching cases registered with the Pimpri Chinchwad police. “He has previous cases, including attempted murder and chain snatching, registered against him. Netke has a case of drug possession against him,” Pawar said.The investigating team included assistant police inspectors Pandurang Devkate, Gorakshnath Balwadkar and Raosaheb Mote, and police sub-inspectors Shivanand Swami and Mahesh Khande.
Article Summary: The police recovered 27 tolas of gold jewellery worth Rs35.33 lakh from the accused, Fida Hussain Irani (33), and his accomplice, Mukesh Netke (38) Irani is wanted in five more chain-snatching cases registered with the Pimpri Chinchwad police.

Article Title: TN man chased, attacked, hacked to death day after seeking police protection; 4 arrested
Article Text:
The deceased, identified as Pradeep Raj of West Mada Street in Tiruvottiyur, was allegedly chased and attacked by the group, sending shockwaves through the area.

Chennai Police tweets





CHENNAI: Four men were arrested for the murder of a 29-year-old man, Pradeep Raj , employed in Chennai harbour, who was hacked to death on West Mada Street in Thiruvottiyur on Wednesday night following a dispute over a Rs 9 lakh loan.Police recovered his body, and it is kept at the morgue in Govt Stanley Hospital.The incident occurred around 8.40 pm in front of a house on West Mada Street.Pradeep Raj, son of Dilli Babu, was walking along the street when a group led by Naveen Kumar, son of Navaneetham, attacked him with knives. He suffered injuries to his head and face and died at the spot.Thiruvottiyur police led by inspector of police Alex traced and arrested Narayanan alias Naveen Kumar (32), Hari Krishnan (21), Jabar (24), and Lokesh (27) from Madhavaram within a few hours after the murder. Police seized knives from the suspects.Police said the murder followed a dispute between the two families over a loan.Pradeep Raj’s mother, Rani, had borrowed Rs 9 lakh from Navaneetham but had not repaid it. When Navaneetham went to demand repayment on July 26, police said Pradeep Raj, Rani, his brother-in-law Sathish, sister Lavanya and father Dilli Babu threatened her.Navaneetham later filed a complaint after consuming thyroid medication and receiving treatment at a private hospital.A case was registered and Pradeep Raj was arrested and remanded in judicial custody. He was subsequently released on station bail.Police said a tense situation prevailed between the two families. Meanwhile, police summoned both parties – Navaneetham and Pradeepraj’s mother Rani – to the Thiruvottiyur police station for an enquiry on Sept 8 over concerns about possible conflict.The cops also gave instructions to both parties to resolve their problem as the cops wanted to have peaceful Vinayagar Chathurthi celebrations.Subsequently, after the enquiry, Pradeep Raj threatened Navaneetham’s family. He also submitted a formal complaint against Navaneetham’s family and sought action against a relative.The four arrested suspects were being interrogated. They will be produced before a court and remanded in judicial custody on Thursday evening.
Article Summary: Pradeep Raj, 29, was walking along the street when a group led by Naveen Kumar, son of Navaneetham, attacked him with knives. He suffered injuries to his head and face and died at the spot. Police seized knives from the suspects.

Article Title: School recognition scam: 177 complaints received so far, CCB informs HC
Article Text:
Chennai:





Central Crime Branch (CCB) police on Wednesday informed Madras high court that it received 177 complaints alleging that money was collected from private schools by promising to obtain permanent recognition, and was subsequently misappropriated.CCB made the submission on a plea moved by one of the accused, Muthukumaran, treasurer of Tamil Nadu Private Schools Association and a former MLA, seeking anticipatory bail apprehending arrest in the case. Recording the submission, Justice V Lakshminarayanan directed CCB to file a counter-affidavit and adjourned the hearing to Sept 10.Based on complaints from schools, CCB registered a case against office-bearers of Tamil Nadu Private Schools Association, including its president B T Arasakumar. On June 27, CCB arrested and detained him under the Goondas Act, based on a complaint by Elangovan, secretary of Federation of Associations of Private Schools in Tamil Nadu.According to the complainant, Arasakumar operated an unregistered organisation under the name ‘Tamil Nadu Private Schools Association’ and claimed that he could obtain approvals — including permanent recognition, DTCP and CMDA approvals, among other statutory permissions — for private schools across the state through his political and official connections.He collected about ₹100 crore from the management of various schools, but failed to secure the approvals or refund the money collected, the complainant said.Arasakumar started off as a DMK functionary, then joined BJP, only to rejoin DMK a few years ago.
Article Summary: CCB made the submission on a plea moved by one of the accused, Muthukumaran, treasurer of Tamil Nadu Private Schools Association. Justice V Lakshminarayanan directed CCB to file a counter-affidavit and adjourned the hearing to Sept 10.

Article Title: Dharapuram bypoll: ‘Election King’ K Padmarajan first to file nomination
Article Text:
K Padmarajan filling his nomination





TIRUPUR: Filing of nominations for the Dharapuram reserved (scheduled caste) assembly bypoll in Tirupur district began at 11am on Wednesday, with self-styled “Election King” K Padmarajan becoming the first candidate to submit papers before revenue divisional officer A Felix Raja. He is contesting as an independent candidatePadmarajan, a tyre shop owner from Attur in Salem district, said this was his 256th nomination since 1988, filed in Tamil Nadu and other states to underline that ordinary citizens could also contest elections. He claimed that the effort was also part of a Guinness record attempt, adding that he had previously contested against leaders including Prime Minister Narendra Modi, former chief ministers J Jayalalithaa, M Karunanidhi and MK Stalin, and chief minister C Joseph Vijay. He had spent lakhs of rupees on filing nominations over the years.According to the election schedule, nominations can be filed till Sept 16. Scrutiny will be held on Sept 17, and the last date for withdrawal is Sept 19. Polling is slated for Oct 6, and counting will be held on Oct 9.The Dharapuram constituency has been a reserved seat since 1967. The constituency has seen shifting electoral outcomes in recent cycles, with AIADMK winning in 2011, Congress in 2016 and DMK in 2021, before the seat returned to AIADMK in the last assembly election.It is for the first time that a bypoll is going to be held in Tirupur district, which was formed in 2009. The bypoll has been necessitated by the resignation of R Sathyabama, who was the sitting MLA. Sathyabhama, who contested on behalf of AIADMK, won the election from Dharapuram constituency by securing 81,100 votes. She voted in support of the TVK during the floor test in the assembly and subsequently resigned from her MLA post and joined the TVK.Meanwhile, DMK on Wednesday announced S Suganya,33, a lawyer and party women’s wing functionary, as its candidate in the constituency.
Article Summary: Self-styled ‘Election King’ K Padmarajan became the first candidate to submit papers. He said this was his 256th nomination since 1988. Polling is slated for Oct 6, and counting will be held on Oct 9.

Article Title: Case against six Bangladeshi nationals for staying Kochi without valid documents
Article Text:

Palarivattom Police has registered a case against six Bangladeshi nationals for allegedly staying in the city without valid passports, visas or other documents authorising their stay.The accused were found living in a rented house in Palarivattom along with two children, aged nine and two-and-a-half years.Those booked are Ibrahim Howlader, 29, Sakeer Khan, 50, Arif Howlader, 29, Unus Khan, 41, Joshana Begum, 30, and Hadiullah Khan, 31, all from Morrelganj in Bagerhat district, Bangladesh.Police said they were arrested during an inspection based on intelligence inputs. They were allegedly working as daily-wage labourers and had been staying in Kochi for about a year. The investigation is under way to determine how they entered India and whether anyone facilitated their stay.

Article Title: Karuvatta murder: Kerala HC stays order allowing police to take minor boys for evidence collection
Article Text:
AI image

Kochi:





The high court has stayed the order of the juvenile justice board (JJB), Alappuzha, permitting the police to take three minor boys, aged 16 and 17, for evidence collection in connection with the murder of a 67-year-old man at Karuvatta in Haripad.A bench of Justice G Gireesh, while granting the stay on Wednesday, sought instructions from the govt and posted the matter for further hearing on Sept 11. The case involves four minors, including the victim’s 13-year-old granddaughter. Three boys, aged between 16 and 17, are accused of carrying out the murder on Aug 15, allegedly at the request of the granddaughter of the deceased.The impugned order, issued by the JJB on Sept 7, allowed the ‘escorted movement’ of the three minors for evidence collection. The revision petition, filed by the children in conflict with the law, challenged the order as patently illegal and argued that it circumvented the statutory bar on police custody of juveniles under Section 10 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015. They contended that the so-called escorted movement was a mere camouflage to secure custodial interrogation for recovery of evidence, a procedure not permitted for minors.The petition further highlighted that the JJB’s order was mechanical and suffered from non-application of mind. It also noted that the board failed to adjudicate on the jurisdictional competence of the investigating officer. The JJB, in its original order, had permitted the police to take the minors for evidence collection, citing that the Juvenile Justice Act is silent on the specific procedure for such custodial interrogation. The prosecution had argued that without the minors’ assistance in evidence collection, the case, which has no eyewitnesses, would be considerably weakened. The board had accepted this contention, resulting in a rare and unprecedented order and prompting the petitioners to approach the HC.
Article Summary: The case involves four minors, including the victim’s 13-year-old granddaughter. Three boys, aged between 16 and 17, are accused of carrying out the murder on Aug 15. The impugned order, issued by the JJB on Sept 7, allowed the ‘escorted movement’ of the three minors for evidence collection.
